Ladakh Orders Spatial Mapping of Changthang Wildlife Sanctuary

2026-09-17 PTI / The Tribune Ladakh, Changthang, wildlife sanctuary, spatial mapping, GIS, GPS, geo-referencing, satellite imagery, boundary review, defence installations
Read the source article

Quick summary

The Ladakh administration has ordered spatial mapping and field verification of the Changthang Cold Desert Wildlife Sanctuary using GPS/GIS and satellite imagery, in a process that balances community rights, wildlife conservation, and national security concerns in a strategic border region.

Key takeaways

  • The Ladakh Lieutenant Governor directed settlement of rights and claims in three protected areas (Hemis National Park, Changthang Wildlife Sanctuary, Karakoram Wildlife Sanctuary) within two months
  • Spatial mapping will use GPS/GIS mapping, geo-referencing, and satellite imagery, with wildlife officials scientifically mapping critical habitats and wildlife movement corridors
  • The sanctuary's strategic border location requires spatial mapping and field surveys of defence installations in coordination with police and defence authorities
  • The previous boundary mapping was done through a "table-top" process without proper ground verification or adherence to the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972
  • The 1987 preliminary notification defining sanctuary boundaries had never been accurately mapped on the ground
  • The sub-committee report was set aside for being inconsistent with legal provisions, inequitable to affected communities, and vulnerable to legal challenges
